title: Stoicism
authors: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (author name not captured)
key_findings: Virtue (perfected reason) is necessary and sufficient for happiness; health, wealth, reputation are 'indifferents'
Some indifferents are 'preferred' (health) and it is appropriate to select them, but they do not decide happiness
Passions (pathe) are excessive impulses from false judgements; the sage has 'good feelings' (eupatheiai); pre-emotions (propatheiai) happen without assent
Assent is 'up to us' in a way that receiving an impression is not
practical_applications: Stoic characters may still prefer health/comfort; the point is not to stake happiness on them
A first flinch of fear is human (pre-emotion); the story beat is what the character assents to next

title: Epictetus (Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
key_findings: Epictetus (c. 55-135 CE), former slave, taught at Nicopolis; wrote nothing; Discourses and Handbook (Enchiridion) come via his student Arrian
Handbook opens: some things are up to us (opinions, impulses, desires, aversions) and some are not (body, possessions, reputation, office)
Prohairesis = faculty of choice/moral character; key practice is testing impressions before assenting
Roles theory: our social 'names' (son, citizen...) point to appropriate acts; life as a play where we do not pick the part
practical_applications: Dichotomy-of-control dialogues for Mint & Tao
Stoicism is role-based and social, not detachment from people
limitations: Year and author of IEP entry not captured
Arrian vs Epictetus authorship debate unresolved

title: Marcus Aurelius
key_findings: Meditations is a private Greek notebook written to himself; title given later by an editor (Casaubon)
Themes: imminence of death, cosmos as a city, acting justly and loving what is allotted, no hatred of others
Draws on Epictetus whom he names
practical_applications: Marcus suits 'notes to self' formats (journal page, pencil notebook) — matches how the text was written
Use his ideas as reminders the character tells themself, not as lectures to others
limitations: First published 2010, revised 2025 per fetch

title: Albert Camus
authors: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (author name not captured)

Myth of Sisyphus ends 'One must imagine Sisyphus happy'; rejects escapes such as hope in an afterlife

title: Existentialism
authors: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (author name not captured)

authors: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (author name not captured)

title: Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta (SN 56.11): Setting the Wheel of Dhamma in Motion
key_findings: Middle way avoids two extremes: sensual indulgence and self-affliction
Dukkha (rendered 'stress') includes birth, aging, death, separation from the loved, not getting what one wants; the five clinging-aggregates
Eightfold path: right view, resolve, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration
practical_applications: Middle way in its original sense; any work-life 'balance' use is an analogy and should be framed as such

title: Anatta-lakkhana Sutta (SN 22.59): The Discourse on the Not-self Characteristic
key_findings: Each aggregate (form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness) is not-self because it leads to affliction and cannot be made to be as one wishes
What is impermanent is unsatisfactory and not fit to be regarded as 'mine, I, my self'
practical_applications: Anatta is about not clinging to aggregates as 'me/mine' — not 'you don't exist'
limitations: Doctrinal; interpretations of anatta differ across schools

title: Viktor Frankl and Logotherapy (Psychology of Adjustment, LibreTexts)

'Last of the human freedoms' = choosing one's attitude

title: Meta-analyses of positive psychology interventions: The effects are much smaller than previously reported
authors: Carmela A. White; Bob Uttl; Mark D. Holder
key_findings: Reanalysis of Sin & Lyubomirsky (2009) and Bolier et al. (2013) correcting for small-sample bias: well-being effect ~ r = .10 (small); depression effects variable, outlier-dependent, mostly non-significant
Calls for larger samples
practical_applications: Do not promise that gratitude lists etc. 'make you happy' — evidence of small effects
limitations: Read via summariser; first half of article

title: Meditation programs for psychological stress and well-being: a systematic review and meta-analysis
key_findings: 47 trials, 3515 participants; small-to-moderate reductions in negative dimensions of stress; mindfulness: moderate evidence for anxiety (ES 0.38 at 8 weeks)
Low/insufficient evidence for positive mood, attention, sleep, weight; not superior to active treatments
practical_applications: Mindfulness claims in captions must stay modest
limitations: PubMed blocked (cookies); details from search snippets

title: Income and emotional well-being: A conflict resolved
authors: Matthew A. Killingsworth; Daniel Kahneman; Barbara Mellers
key_findings: Adversarial collaboration: happiness rises with log(income) for most; plateau only among the least happy group (~$100k)

practical_applications: Money-happiness claims: nuanced, not 'money can't buy happiness'
